authority: Evidence Integration upstream collection and analytic hypothesis preservation only; no Claims Forensics adjudication and no public finding
topic: October 4 Mehrabad dark-transport cluster and possible extraction of IRGC personnel from Yemen
chain_rule: Preserve observed aviation events, reported prior IRGC insertion, counteroffensive timing, hypotheses and alternatives as separate nodes. Sequence and temporal proximity do not establish common mission, origin, passenger identity or extraction.

event_chain.event: Reuters reported from four sources that a July 13 Mahan Air flight diverted from Sanaa to Hodeidah carried 10-21 IRGC personnel, including commanders/advisers, plus missile/drone-related equipment. Iran and the Houthis denied military personnel or aid were aboard.
event_chain.status: MULTISOURCE_REUTERS_REPORT_WITH_OFFICIAL_DENIAL; already preserved in ATLAS Yemen/Mahan chain

event_chain.event: Shin/FromIran recorded an IRIAF C-130 landing at Mehrabad, alongside an earlier unidentified Il-76 arrival.
event_chain.status: OSINT_OBSERVATION; establishes a recent ordinary IRIAF C-130 presence/arrival base rate at Mehrabad and is not evidence of Yemen linkage

event_chain.event: Shin/FromIran reported a C-130 landing at Tehran Mehrabad with its transponder off.
event_chain.status: OBSERVED_ARRIVAL_ONLY; operator, tail number, origin, prior route, cargo and passengers not established

event_chain.event: Shin/FromIran reported a Mahan Air B747 descending toward Mehrabad with its transponder off 13 minutes after the reported C-130 arrival.
event_chain.status: OBSERVED_TEMPORAL_PROXIMITY_ONLY; no common mission, route, passenger or Yemen connection established

event_chain.event: Shin/FromIran later reported another unidentified aircraft with its transponder off circling in from the south before landing at Mehrabad.
event_chain.status: OBSERVED_ARRIVAL_DIRECTION_ONLY; aircraft identity, origin and relation to the earlier transports unresolved

event_chain.event: Yemen's Saudi-backed internationally recognized government publicly announced a major campaign to retake Houthi-held territory, moving the previously reported offensive from planning to execution.
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces reported major gains around Bab el-Mandeb, Dhubab and toward Mocha. Reuters could not independently verify the full extent and Houthis rejected the claims.

hypotheses.proposition: The October 4 C-130 arrival at Mehrabad may have been part of an operation extracting IRGC commanders/advisers from Yemen before or during the Saudi-backed Yemeni counteroffensive.
supporting_considerations: ATLAS already preserves multisource reporting that IRGC commanders/advisers were flown into Houthi-controlled Yemen in July.
The unidentified C-130 arrived shortly before the Yemen counteroffensive was publicly announced as underway and before reported government gains accelerated.
Iran would have a rational force-protection incentive to reduce exposure of scarce experienced expeditionary personnel once the Saudi-backed operation and outside support became apparent.
evidence_against_or_limiting_weight: No tail number, operator, departure airport, route, intermediate stop, manifest, passenger imagery or passenger-source reporting has been established for the October 4 C-130.
Mehrabad has recent documented IRIAF C-130 activity, creating a strong domestic logistics/base-rate alternative.
The Mahan B747 arrival 13 minutes later is only temporal proximity; no evidence establishes a shared mission.
The later aircraft arriving from the south is unidentified and may be unrelated.
No credible public source reviewed here says IRGC personnel were withdrawn from Yemen on October 4.
promotion_criteria: Identify the October 4 C-130 airframe or operator and reconstruct a prior leg from Yemen or a plausible Yemen-linked staging point.
Obtain credible reporting, imagery or records placing IRGC Yemen personnel on the aircraft or documenting a contemporaneous withdrawal.
Establish a Hodeidah, Sanaa or Yemen-linked intermediate-airfield movement that can be temporally chained to the Mehrabad arrival.
disconfirmation_criteria: Conclusive airframe/route evidence showing an unrelated domestic Iranian mission.
Credible passenger/cargo documentation establishing another mission.
Independent evidence placing the relevant IRGC Yemen command contingent in Yemen after the October 4 arrival window without a separate rotation explanation.

hypotheses.proposition: The October 4 C-130 was an ordinary or war-related domestic IRIAF logistics movement unrelated to Yemen.
supporting_considerations: IRIAF C-130 activity at Mehrabad was directly observed days earlier.
No origin or passenger evidence ties the October 4 aircraft to Yemen.

evidence_links.relevance: Prior reported IRGC commander/adviser insertion into Houthi-controlled Yemen and official denial.
October 4 C-130 Mehrabad arrival at 0903Z with transponder off.
October 4 Mahan Air B747 descent toward Mehrabad at 0916Z with transponder off.
Later October 4 unidentified transponder-off aircraft arriving from the south.
September 28 IRIAF C-130 arrival at Mehrabad, preserving the domestic/base-rate alternative.
October 4 transition of the Saudi-backed Yemeni counteroffensive from planning to publicly announced execution.
October 5 reported Bab el-Mandeb/Dhubab/Mocha gains with Reuters verification caveat and Houthi denial.

routing.evidence_integration: Preserve as a linked aviation/Yemen evidence chain and continue airframe, route, passenger and post-October-4 IRGC-presence collection. Do not promote extraction as fact without discriminating evidence.
routing.claims_forensics: No Lie Ledger proposition is created merely from this hypothesis. Consume only if a public actor makes a falsifiable claim about the aircraft, withdrawal, continued IRGC presence or Yemen direction; preserve exact wording and time.
routing.public_product: No direct publication authority. If surfaced as an unresolved intelligence note, label origin/operator/passengers unknown and separate observed facts from analytic hypothesis.

unresolved_questions: What was the October 4 C-130 tail number and operator?
Where did it depart immediately before Mehrabad, and were there earlier legs through Hodeidah, Sanaa, southern Iran, Oman or another staging point?
Was the October 4 Mahan B747 movement operationally related to the C-130 or merely coincident?

Can satellite imagery, local imagery, Mode-S/MLAT archives or airfield observations identify relevant October 3-4 activity at Hodeidah, Sanaa, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar or other plausible staging locations?
Is there credible post-October-4 evidence placing the previously reported IRGC command/advisory contingent still in Yemen?
limitations: No proprietary ADS-B/Mode-S archive or commercial satellite terminal was available for this referral.
No origin, route, tail number or passenger identity is inferred from a transponder-off arrival alone.
Temporal proximity to the counteroffensive is evidentiary context, not proof of causation or mission.
The October 4 Mahan B747 and later unidentified aircraft are not treated as part of one operation absent independent linkage.
